title: A King Asks for Rescue and Peace
overview: A king praises God as his protection in war, admits how brief human life is, asks God to rescue him from lying enemies, and pictures the peace and plenty that would follow.

parts.label: God as the king's protection (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The speaker, traditionally King David, piles up images of safety (rock, fortress, shield) and credits God with his skill in battle and his authority over people. Many lines closely echo Psalm 18, so this psalm seems to reuse older royal songs.

parts.label: How small humans are (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: In the middle of confident praise, the king wonders why God pays attention to people at all, since a human life is like a breath or a passing shadow. Psalm 8 asks a similar question, but there it leads to human dignity and here it leads to frailty.

parts.label: A plea for God to come down (vv. 5-8)
parts.note: The king asks God to arrive like a great storm, with smoking mountains and lightning as arrows, imagery that recalls God appearing at Mount Sinai. The enemies are foreigners whose 'right hand' is false; people raised the right hand to swear an oath, so this means they break their promises.

parts.label: A new song for rescue (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: The king promises a fresh song of thanks on a ten-stringed instrument and credits God with every victory kings win. He then repeats his request to be saved from the sword and from the lying enemies.

parts.label: A picture of peace (vv. 12-15)
parts.note: The psalm ends with a thriving nation: strong sons like young plants, daughters like finely carved stonework in a palace, full barns, growing herds, no breach in the city walls and no cry of distress in the streets. Scholars are unsure how this connects to the earlier prayer, and it may once have been a separate piece, but it presents this good life as the result of belonging to the LORD.

think: If human life really is as brief as a breath, what do you think makes it matter, and what would a good life for a whole community need to include?
